Watts to Amps at 240V — Dryers, EVs, and High Power Guide

Single-phase AC path

Current, voltage, and power factor feeding a real watt result

AC pages need power factor context, so the visual connects outlet voltage, current draw, PF, and breaker planning.

Formula Amps = Watts / (240V x PF)

Quick answer

Use this calculator to convert AC current into real watts with voltage and power factor.

Single-phase AC loads can be resistive or inductive. Resistive loads may be near PF 1.00, while motors, compressors, and HVAC equipment often need a lower power factor.

Amps = Watts / (240V x PF)

Inputs to check before calculating

  • Use the correct nominal voltage for the circuit.
  • Enter measured current or nameplate running current.
  • Use realistic PF for motors, compressors, and transformer loads.
  • Compare the result with breaker and continuous-load limits.

Example: 1,200 watts at 240 volts

At 240 volts, a 1,200 watt load draws 5 amps before AC power-factor adjustments. Use the power factor field when the equipment is a motor, compressor, inverter, or other inductive load.

Best use cases

  • Dryers and EV chargers
  • High-power circuits
  • PF-aware current
  • single-phase AC load planning with clear unit labels.

Common mistake to avoid

Do not use DC-style amps x volts for every AC load when the equipment has a lower power factor.

How to use the result

Use the watt result for appliance planning, branch-circuit checks, and comparison with the main amps to watts formula.

Accuracy and safety note

Calculator output is a planning estimate. Final breaker sizing, wire gauge, derating, voltage-drop limits, equipment protection, and code compliance should be verified with manufacturer documentation and a qualified electrician or engineer.

For the broad formula, reference table, and breaker planning context, start with the main Amps to Watts Calculator.

FAQ

Watts to Amps at 240V — Dryers, EV FAQ

Fast answers before you use the calculator or compare formulas.

30A How many watts is 30 amps at 240V?

30 amps at 240V equals 7,200 watts (30 × 240 = 7,200). This is a common circuit for electric dryers and some EV chargers. The 80% continuous load limit is 5,760 watts.

BRK What size breaker do I need for a 240V circuit?

Divide the appliance wattage by 240 to find amps, then choose the next standard breaker size. A 5,500W dryer: 5,500 ÷ 240 = 22.9A → 30A breaker. A 7,680W EV charger: 7,680 ÷ 240 = 32A → 40A breaker (with 80% rule: 32A is 80% of 40A).

WHY Why is 240V used for large appliances in the US?

The US electrical system provides both 120V and 240V from a split-phase transformer. 240V delivers twice the wattage at the same amperage, allowing smaller wire and breaker sizes for high-power loads. A 5,500W dryer on 120V would need 46A and thick cable; on 240V, it needs only 23A.

PH Is US 240V single-phase or two-phase?

US residential 240V is technically single-phase, split into two 120V legs that are 180° out of phase. It is sometimes called "split-phase" but not "two-phase." True two-phase and three-phase systems use different transformer configurations and are found in commercial/industrial settings.

EV How do I calculate EV charger amps from watts at 240V?

Divide charger watts by 240V. A Level 2 EV charger rated at 7,680W draws 7,680 ÷ 240 = 32 amps. For the 80% NEC continuous load rule, this needs a 40A breaker (32 ÷ 0.80 = 40) and 8 AWG copper wire for typical residential runs.

⚠ Can I convert a 120V outlet to 240V?

Only if the circuit has the proper wiring. A 240V circuit needs two hot wires, a neutral (if 120V taps are needed), and a ground. A licensed electrician must install the correct breaker, receptacle, and verify the wire gauge is adequate for the planned load. Never attempt to combine two 120V circuits into 240V without proper rewiring.
